doors.note: Bedroom doors (bedroom to corridor) and en-suite doors follow their own rules (docs/02). The day-room doors are fire doors on hold-open devices, as in HM Government's 'Fire safety risk assessment: residential care premises' (2006), and are closed overnight. The staff room is kept closed for privacy; the exit is on a keypad.

sources.max_opening_mm: HSE, 'Falls from windows or balconies in health and social care' (HSIS 5): windows people could fall from are restricted, 'to 100 mm or less' (https://www.hse.gov.uk/healthservices/falls-windows.htm)
sources.open_min_temp_c, open_max_wind_mps, clos: Assumptions in the v1.0-testbed spec, approved by the project owner (2026-10-01): staff air a room after morning care on a mild, dry, calm day and close it again within the half hour or at bedtime

sources.dark_below_wm2: Assumption (v1.0-testbed PR 2): about the outdoor light of a heavily overcast morning or late afternoon, when indoor lights go on
sources.corridor_dim: The wing's night lights (docs/02), on the same hours as the fire doors

sources.setpoint_c: Project owner, v1.0-testbed spec decision 7 (2026-10-01): 22 °C in day rooms, 21 °C in bedrooms (en-suites with their bedroom)
sources.season: Assumption: UK heating season, October to April
